title: Example game (test fixture)
summary: Tiny fixture used by validator and engine tests. Never built into the public site.

items.misconception: Same ingredients means the same chain
items.prompt: Two bead chains use the same three colors, but in a different order. Are their sequences the same?

choices.text: Yes, same colors means same sequence
choices.feedback: Composition is the same, but sequence is the order. A different order is a different sequence.

choices.text: Nobody can tell from colors alone
choices.feedback: We can tell: the order of the beads is visible, and it differs.

items.explanation: Sequence is the ordered list of residues, so the same composition in another order is a different sequence.
hint_ladder: Look at which bead comes first in each chain.
Sequence is about order, not just which colors are present.

items.misconception: A chain reads the same from either end
items.prompt: A peptide chain has a defined direction. Which statement fits that?

choices.text: It runs from the amino (N) terminus toward the carboxyl (C) terminus
Either end can be called the start; the chain is symmetric
choices.feedback: The two ends are chemically different (amino vs carboxyl), so the chain has a direction.

choices.text: Direction is only a drawing convention with no chemical basis
choices.feedback: Reading N to C is a convention, but it follows a real chemical difference between the ends.

items.explanation: The N and C termini differ chemically, which is why sequences are written N to C.
hint_ladder: Think about the two named ends of the chain.
The ends are not chemically identical.

items.misconception: Sequence alone predicts what a peptide does
items.prompt: Why is primary sequence not a stand-alone prediction of biological activity?

choices.text: Side-chain chemistry, conformation, modifications, environment and target all matter
Sequence has no influence on activity
choices.feedback: Sequence does constrain chemistry; it is just not sufficient on its own.

choices.text: It is a full prediction once the order is known
choices.feedback: Order is necessary information but not sufficient; context and target also matter.

items.explanation: Sequence constrains behavior but activity also depends on conformation, modifications, environment and the target.
